Child Protection Register II [5651]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Child Protection Register

When we did programme in 2016 there was 1 number on the register…after news pressure at the time they said they were working on it and had extended to 24.

In 2019 there were on 509 names on the Child Protection Register.

140 029 names were checked against register, despite the fact that there are 410 000 teachers in SA. All schools can’t be checking the register.

Does the Register work at all.

Can it protect our children?

Two recent murders of children in Cape Town and the question of the efficacy Child Protection Register has surfaced again.

We don’t have enough police to protect every street corner. The register may work at schools where teachers work with children, if they are checked against it.

But after school there is little or no protection. Should register be made public. Don’t the community have a right to know who is living in their area. Are rights of criminals more important that protecting our children.

In America the perpetrators have to inform the community.
What about violent vigilantism in South Africa.
What is fair?


Interviewees

Tazne van Wyk family 8 Cape Town Elsies Rivier
Tazne’s body was found outside Worcester. Her neighbour Moyhdian Pangarker pointed out the location of her body in a stormwater drain. He has since been charged with her murder.
Tazne had been missing for almost two weeks after last being seen walking to the tuck shop across the road from her home in Connaught Estate on February 7.
Pangarker had been a person of interest in her kidnapping. He was arrested in Cradock last Tuesday.
News24 Footage of funeral, Ramaphosa, Bheki Cele and Chris Nissen


Reagan Gertse family 7 Cape Town

A 7-year-old boy murdered in Tubagh will be laid to rest on Saturday.
Reagan Gertse was found dead last weekend.
Police have arrested a parolee who lives two doors away from the deceased's family and is a distant relative.
Mourners will gather at the Old Apostolic Church in the Cape Winelands community of Tulbagh on Saturday morning to bid a final farewell to Gertse.
The 7-year-old boy's body was found on the banks of a river on Sunday - just hours after he was reported missing.
The accused - 58-year-old Jakobus Petoors - is the victim's step-grandfather's brother - and lives only two doors away from the slain child's family.
Petoors - who was released on parole in November - has been charged with Gertse's rape and murder.


Sheena Swemmer - JHB
is an attorney and Head of the Gender Programme at the Centre for Applied Legal Studies, Wits University.
General failure of systems
Victims don’t come forward
Under reported
What is on register is just tip of the iceberg
Doesn’t think that it should be made public due to vigilantism.
We have no way of ensuring that places are safe.
More of a burden on parents to make sure child OK.
Cannot police every corner.
In prison punished but not rehabilitated.

People are surprsied when they re offend but given no rehabilitation in prison.

(Not sure that child sex offenders can be rehabilitated.)

Chris Nissen – SAHRC - spoke at funeral
Community Protection Unit needs to know when someone like this is coming into area.
The Police Station comander needs to know when someone come into area.
The community needs to be consulted when someone like that is released into community. We cannot release characters like that without us knowing who is coming into our community. What is community doing to keep community safe. We need to be proactive. Community stand up and speak out. Enough is enough, but we must do things ourselves. Don’t just look at the government. Unite and build the community. My child is your child and we must look after each other.

Benita Moolman – Cape Town
Benita Moolman is a Research Specialist in the Human and Social Development Unit . She holds an M (Phil) in Women and Gender Studies at the University of the Western Cape and obtained a PhD in Feminist Geography from the University of California, Davis in the United States.
Has worked with sex offenders.


Minister of Social Development – Lindiwe Sisulu
Request an interview.
Why so few people checked?
Are they making sure people check against register?
Independent schools say it takes a long time to check.
Need to cheack once a year.


Chrispin Phiri – Spokesperson for Minister of Justice
(In our last programme we spoke to Tlali Tlali.)
It just isnt working is it?
Does not really protect children?
Perhaps at school but not after?
Good law on paper but little use in real world?


Marcel Londt

Interviewed her in last programme. She arranged for us to speak to sex offender. We do not know that people on parole had convictions against them of sex with children.
I do wonder if the children they raped and killed were just easy targets.
Not sure if she will speak again.
She referred me to Bonita Moolman.
Do we want to speak to a child molester?

Script:


The Paedophile Next Door


V/O
Beatrice Williams is the mother of 3 children and lives in Pelican Park on the Cape Flats. Had she known that a convicted paedophile was living a couple of houses away, her 12 year old daughter Michaela might still be alive today.

Beatrice
“At any other day, Michaela was playing around in the courtyard outside with her friends.

V/O
Michaela came in for supper after playing with her friends outside.

Beatrice
She asked me what did I make? And I told her I made vetkoek and she was so excited because she asked me to make vetkoek for so long.”

V/O
Beatrice remembers how happy she was to hear the children laughing in the courtyard while she took a bath

Beatrice
“When I got done I did not hear anybody anymore.

V/O
She sensed something was wrong , the other children were there, but Michaela was missing. She frantically started searching for her daughter.

Beatrice
Ever since that time I never saw her again.”

Link MASA TO CHANGE LINE IN LINK
Hundreds of fatal child abuse cases are reported in South Africa annually for 2018/2019 period 1014 children were killed - an increase of 2.9% from the previous year.

V/O
In the same year there were over 24 thousand sexual offences against children reported to the police. That averages about 66 a day.

Sheena Swemmer for the Centre for Applied Legal Studies says these stats don’t reflect the full picture.







Sheena
“If people don’t have faith in police or courts, they are not going to come forward and report crime, so that is why giving a number to you is probably too small, its severly underestimated how many attacks are happening against children.
You should think of children as being right there as some of the most vulnerable people in our society that are facing constant violence.

V/O
Beatrice never saw her daughter again.

Candice
“This is where Michaela Williams body was found, there was actually a tree stump laying across here and her body was in front of the tree stump buried under branches and rubble.

V/O
Candice van der Rheede founded the Western Cape Missing Persons Unit 3 years ago. With a group of about 100 volunteers , they scoured the area to find Michaela’s body. Her organisation also feeds children and educates them about their rights.

Candice
“For me it is very emotional.This is where the child took her last breath this is where a young life was stolen.”

Beatrice
“As I heard people said she was raped and strangled . But me myself but I couldn’t bring myself to open a newspaper to read what has happened to my child, even though I want to know…..cries.”

V/O
The paedophile was known to the family. Michaela was his second victim. In 2005 he raped and brutally stabbed an 8 year old in the heart with a pair of scissors and left her for dead.

Masa
“Did the community know that he had a criminal record and was out on parole?”

Candice
“They were under the impression that the killer of Michaela Wiliams was in prison for car theft. For in actual fact he was in prison for the rape and attempted murder of an 8 year old child. And of that sentence that he had gotten, he only served 13 years.”

V/O
The angry community came out in force when the accused appeared in the Wynberg Magistrate's court a couple of days later.


Up Sound
“How can you release a man that has raped before?”

Masa
“Beatrice do you think if you had known about the 2005 crime that he had comitted do you think he would have been treated differently by the community?”

Beatrice
“I think people would have been more cautious about him , they wouldn’t have allowed their children around him. I wouldn’t even have allowed him in my house.”

V/O
The Children’s Act of 2005 makes provision for a Child Protection Register. This is a list of all of the people who have comitted crimes against children and who are no longer permitted to work with children and vulnerable adults.
This list is held by the Department of Social Development and it cannot be accessed by the public.

Masa
“Now if parolees are let back into society can these lists help to protect our children?”

Sheena Swemmer
“So no. Not unless the parolee is going to be working with a child, also no because who can even access these lists so I would say no because your parolee will no necessarily be getting a formal jobs working with children. Your aquaintances your families and these registers are focussed on employees.”

V/O
Michaela’s murderer may have been on the register but no one in the community would have been able to access it.

V/O
We’ve been following this story of the implementation of the Child Protection Register for nearly a decade.

V/O
In 2011 Social Development Mininster Bathabile Dlamini said that the Child Protection Register only had one name on it, even though there were nearly 54 000 reported crimes against children that year.

And 9 years later, the number of offenders on the register has grown to a paltry 1660.





Masa
“Now when one considers the number of sexual crimes again children, that number is awfully low.”


Sheena
“With regards to sexual offences generally only 8% of cases that were reported actually end up in a conviction.”

V/O
This means that there are many sex offenders living amongst us.

UCT’s Dr Benita Moolman and says the likelihood of sex offenders is high.

Masa
“When paedophiles are incarcerated is there any reabilitation programmes?”

Benita
“Very very few. They often talk about 3 years as a minimum treatment programme for sex offenders and then it is a life long monitoring of sex offenders that need to happen and so there is various theories or appriaches. One that I think is useful to talk about is the one one that is similar to addiction where you are always a recovering alcoholic and so similarly sex offenders need to be viewed in that way.”

Link
“In America the Sexual Offender Register is open everyone can access it, convicted sex offenders have to inform the police when they move into an area

V/O
It’s as easy as typing in an address and you can see which sex offenders live in your neighbourhood.

V/O
Tazne van Wyk’s family did not know that they were living on the same street as as a child murderer.

Exactly one month after Micaela Williams was brutally murdered, and only 20 km away, 8 year old Tazne also went missing. Her body was found 2 weeks later, she was kidnapped and murdered by 54 year old Moeyhdien Pangarker.

Her parents Carmen van Wyk and Terence Manuel are still severely traumatised.

Marcel
“She was only 8 years old, 8 years old, she was my baby my everything.”


V/O
The two murders enraged the community.
President Cyril Ramaphosa came to personally pay his respects to Tazne’s family.

Up Sound
“I stand here as the government to say sorry a person who was never meant to be released on parole was released.”

Carmen
“The system failed, all these years it has failed.”

V/O
With two very similar murders within a month of each other, the community feared for the safety of their children.

Dan Plato
“What a sad day that another mother and father that are burying their loving child.”

Chris Nissen
“We need to be consulted when a person like that is released into that community, we cannot release characters like that into the community without us knowing who is coming for our community.”

Masa
“So you didn’t know anything more about him whether he was on parole for any other crime?”

Carmen
“ We didn’t know anything about him.”

Terence
“We knew nothing, we would have kept our child away from him from that house obviously.”

V/O
Shaheda Omar of the Teddy Bear Clinic says they have seen more than 200 cases of abuse of children at home during lockdown.


Masa
“When a sexual offender moves into an area has the community got the right to know?”

Shaheda
“Ideally yes, first prize to know is the person suitable to live in neighbourhood, is my child gong to be safe playing in the streets but unfortunately that is not the reality.”




V/O
So should the Child Protection Register be made public to protect South African children?

Candice
“Well there are two sides to that story if it was made public, one the public would rather take the law into their own hands and start victimising the perpetrators. So what I would suggest is that they do make it public but only to law enforcement agencies, local CPF and neighbourhood watches.”

V/O
Carmen and Terence are unemployed and resent that the man who took their child’s life is protected and having three meals a day behind bars.

Carmen
“Up till now he still get his human rights, after he took our child’s rights away from her. Where was her human rights at that time?”

Shaheda
“So there is a breakdown in the system things are not working its not a well oiled machine, unfortunately a lot of work needs to be done and the resources that are allocated are definitely not sufficient.”

Benita
“We need to move beyond just calling for harsher penalties, we need to see community monitoring programmes in place that government is comitted to to prevent sexual violence.”


Beatrice
“I don’t want to sound rude or anything but look at what we are going through now, this lockdown. Such a big effort was put in to keep our people safe my question is just when are they going to put in this much effort to keep our children safe.”

Legally Ok’ed promos

Promo 1
Within a month of each other two young girls, aged 8 and 12, were brutally raped and murdered by hardened criminals who were out on parole. How do we protect children when the system fails?


Promo 2
How do you know if a convicted child sex offender moves into your area? With the Child Protection Register not accessible to the public, should communities have more say about who lives amongst them?

Promo 3
Would public access to a sex offenders register help communities protect children from convicted paedophiles and child abusers living in the same area?

One that I think is useful to talk about is the one one that is similar to addiction where you are always a recovering alcoholic and so similarly sex offenders need to be viewed in that way.” Link “In America the Sexual Offender Register is open everyone can access it, convicted sex offenders have to inform the police when they move into an area V/O It’s as easy as typing in an address and you can see which sex offenders live in your neighbourhood. V/O Tazne van Wyk’s family did not know that they were living on the same street as as a child murderer. Exactly one month after Micaela Williams was brutally murdered, and only 20 km away, 8 year old Tazne also went missing. Her body was found 2 weeks later, she was kidnapped and murdered by 54 year old Moeyhdien Pangarker. Her parents Carmen van Wyk and Terence Manuel are still severely traumatised. Marcel “She was only 8 years old, 8 years old, she was my baby my everything.” V/O The two murders enraged the community. President Cyril Ramaphosa came to personally pay his respects to Tazne’s family. Up Sound “I stand here as the government to say sorry a person who was never meant to be released on parole was released.” Carmen “The system failed, all these years it has failed.” V/O With two very similar murders within a month of each other, the community feared for the safety of their children. Dan Plato “What a sad day that another mother and father that are burying their loving child.” Chris Nissen “We need to be consulted when a person like that is released into that community, we cannot release characters like that into the community without us knowing who is coming for our community.” Masa “So you didn’t know anything more about him whether he was on parole for any other crime?” Carmen “ We didn’t know anything about him.” Terence “We knew nothing, we would have kept our child away from him from that house obviously.” V/O Shaheda Omar of the Teddy Bear Clinic says they have seen more than 200 cases of abuse of children at home during lockdown. Masa “When a sexual offender moves into an area has the community got the right to know?” Shaheda “Ideally yes, first prize to know is the person suitable to live in neighbourhood, is my child gong to be safe playing in the streets but unfortunately that is not the reality.” V/O So should the Child Protection Register be made public to protect South African children? Candice “Well there are two sides to that story if it was made public, one the public would rather take the law into their own hands and start victimising the perpetrators. So what I would suggest is that they do make it public but only to law enforcement agencies, local CPF and neighbourhood watches.” V/O Carmen and Terence are unemployed and resent that the man who took their child’s life is protected and having three meals a day behind bars. Carmen “Up till now he still get his human rights, after he took our child’s rights away from her. Where was her human rights at that time?” Shaheda “So there is a breakdown in the system things are not working its not a well oiled machine, unfortunately a lot of work needs to be done and the resources that are allocated are definitely not sufficient.” Benita “We need to move beyond just calling for harsher penalties, we need to see community monitoring programmes in place that government is comitted to to prevent sexual violence.” Beatrice “I don’t want to sound rude or anything but look at what we are going through now, this lockdown. Such a big effort was put in to keep our people safe my question is just when are they going to put in this much effort to keep our children safe.” Legally Ok’ed promos Promo 1 Within a month of each other two young girls, aged 8 and 12, were brutally raped and murdered by hardened criminals who were out on parole. How do we protect children when the system fails? Promo 2 How do you know if a convicted child sex offender moves into your area? With the Child Protection Register not accessible to the public, should communities have more say about who lives amongst them? Promo 3 Would public access to a sex offenders register help communities protect children from convicted paedophiles and child abusers living in the same area?

metadata.Further information: Child Protection Register When we did programme in 2016 there was 1 number on the register…after news pressure at the time they said they were working on it and had extended to 24. In 2019 there were on 509 names on the Child Protection Register. 140 029 names were checked against register, despite the fact that there are 410 000 teachers in SA. All schools can’t be checking the register. Does the Register work at all. Can it protect our children? Two recent murders of children in Cape Town and the question of the efficacy Child Protection Register has surfaced again. We don’t have enough police to protect every street corner. The register may work at schools where teachers work with children, if they are checked against it. But after school there is little or no protection. Should register be made public. Don’t the community have a right to know who is living in their area. Are rights of criminals more important that protecting our children. In America the perpetrators have to inform the community. What about violent vigilantism in South Africa. What is fair? Interviewees Tazne van Wyk family 8 Cape Town Elsies Rivier Tazne’s body was found outside Worcester. Her neighbour Moyhdian Pangarker pointed out the location of her body in a stormwater drain. He has since been charged with her murder. Tazne had been missing for almost two weeks after last being seen walking to the tuck shop across the road from her home in Connaught Estate on February 7. Pangarker had been a person of interest in her kidnapping. He was arrested in Cradock last Tuesday. News24 Footage of funeral, Ramaphosa, Bheki Cele and Chris Nissen Reagan Gertse family 7 Cape Town A 7-year-old boy murdered in Tubagh will be laid to rest on Saturday. Reagan Gertse was found dead last weekend. Police have arrested a parolee who lives two doors away from the deceased's family and is a distant relative. Mourners will gather at the Old Apostolic Church in the Cape Winelands community of Tulbagh on Saturday morning to bid a final farewell to Gertse. The 7-year-old boy's body was found on the banks of a river on Sunday - just hours after he was reported missing. The accused - 58-year-old Jakobus Petoors - is the victim's step-grandfather's brother - and lives only two doors away from the slain child's family. Petoors - who was released on parole in November - has been charged with Gertse's rape and murder. Sheena Swemmer - JHB is an attorney and Head of the Gender Programme at the Centre for Applied Legal Studies, Wits University. General failure of systems Victims don’t come forward Under reported What is on register is just tip of the iceberg Doesn’t think that it should be made public due to vigilantism. We have no way of ensuring that places are safe. More of a burden on parents to make sure child OK. Cannot police every corner. In prison punished but not rehabilitated. People are surprsied when they re offend but given no rehabilitation in prison. (Not sure that child sex offenders can be rehabilitated.) Chris Nissen – SAHRC - spoke at funeral Community Protection Unit needs to know when someone like this is coming into area. The Police Station comander needs to know when someone come into area. The community needs to be consulted when someone like that is released into community. We cannot release characters like that without us knowing who is coming into our community. What is community doing to keep community safe. We need to be proactive. Community stand up and speak out. Enough is enough, but we must do things ourselves. Don’t just look at the government. Unite and build the community. My child is your child and we must look after each other. Benita Moolman – Cape Town Benita Moolman is a Research Specialist in the Human and Social Development Unit . She holds an M (Phil) in Women and Gender Studies at the University of the Western Cape and obtained a PhD in Feminist Geography from the University of California, Davis in the United States. Has worked with sex offenders. Minister of Social Development – Lindiwe Sisulu Request an interview. Why so few people checked? Are they making sure people check against register? Independent schools say it takes a long time to check. Need to cheack once a year. Chrispin Phiri – Spokesperson for Minister of Justice (In our last programme we spoke to Tlali Tlali.) It just isnt working is it? Does not really protect children? Perhaps at school but not after? Good law on paper but little use in real world? Marcel Londt Interviewed her in last programme. She arranged for us to speak to sex offender. We do not know that people on parole had convictions against them of sex with children. I do wonder if the children they raped and killed were just easy targets. Not sure if she will speak again. She referred me to Bonita Moolman. Do we want to speak to a child molester?
